title: System design – local design canvas
description: Local canvas where agents add architecture steps over MCP and a reviewer walks them in the browser. Designs are JSON files on disk.

steps.title: Existing app plus a production server and CI
steps.summary: Records the architecture as it stands (browser app, Vite-hosted API, MCP server, JSON files) and adds a standalone Node server that serves the built app and the same API without Vite, a format version on design files, and a CI workflow.

steps.title: Drift check against compose, Kubernetes and Terraform
steps.summary: Adds Terraform JSON to the infrastructure reader and a drift check that reuses the import in sync mode: it reports what the infrastructure has and the design lacks, and can add it as a step for review. Exposed as a CI CLI and the sync_infra MCP tool.

steps.title: Shareable read-only HTML file
steps.summary: Exports a design (plus the designs its parts open) as one self-contained HTML file: the built app with script and styles inlined and the designs baked in as JSON. In that file the client API switches to an in-memory store, so it runs from disk or any static host with no server.

steps.title: Capacity checks and failure impact
steps.summary: Parts get an optional capacity (req/s). Lint compares it with the qps on incoming lines; a failure analysis walks the graph from entry points without a part to find broken flows and parts cut off. Shown in the inspector and exposed to agents as simulate_failure.

steps.title: Drift tracks part sources and removals
steps.summary: Imported parts now record their source (format and infra key). Drift matches on it first, so renames survive, and reports parts once imported from that format that the infrastructure dropped; sync removes them in the review step. Terraform links now walk through undrawn resources and wiring (listeners, target groups, event source mappings) while skipping shared plumbing.

steps.title: Export to Structurizr, C4-PlantUML and draw.io
steps.summary: Adds text exports for other architecture tools so teams can try this one without leaving theirs: Structurizr DSL and C4-PlantUML at C4 container level, and a draw.io file with sheet positions. Same code serves the Export menu and the export_design MCP tool.

steps.title: Tag views over one model
steps.summary: Parts carry free tags; a View menu shows one tag at a time, hiding the rest of the parts, their lines, attached notes and boxes left empty. Agents set tags through add_step, add_component and update_component.

steps.title: Import OpenTelemetry and Jaeger traces
steps.summary: The infra reader also accepts recorded traces (OTLP JSON or a Jaeger download). Services, databases, queues and outside hosts become parts. Calls become lines with measured qps and one-way latency. Each kind of request becomes a flow. Drift reports lines whose numbers are off by more than a quarter.

steps.title: Paste any diagram as a step
steps.summary: There is now a single importer that recognises the format. It reads Mermaid (flowchart, sequence, C4, architecture-beta), C4-PlantUML, compose, Kubernetes, Terraform and traces. It is reached by pasting on the canvas or through the MCP import_diagram tool. Each import becomes a new step and reuses parts by name. Copying parts writes a Mermaid flowchart to the clipboard.

notes.text: Binds 127.0.0.1 by default; PORT and HOST override. Unknown paths fall back to index.html.
Removals only touch parts whose source is the same format; hand-drawn parts and parts from another infra file are never removed.

decisions.title: Plain node:http server for production instead of keeping Vite
decisions.why: The app could only run inside the Vite dev server. A small node:http server serves dist/ and mounts the same createApi() handler, so dev and prod share one API code path with no new dependency.
alternatives: Run vite preview with the plugin
decisions.tradeoffs: Static serving (types, caching, traversal guard) is hand-written and minimal; no compression or HTTPS. Fine for a local tool bound to 127.0.0.1.

decisions.title: Version field on design files with migrate-on-read
decisions.why: Files had no format version, so a future schema change would make old designs fail validation. parseDesign now treats unversioned files as v1, runs migrations up to the current version, and refuses files from a newer version instead of misreading them.
alternatives: No versioning, keep schema fields optional forever
decisions.tradeoffs: Files are upgraded only when next written, so the folder can hold mixed versions until then.

decisions.title: Read Terraform from `terraform show -json`, not HCL source
decisions.why: The JSON output is Terraform's stable machine format, carries resolved names, depends_on and (in plans) expression references, and the existing YAML parser already reads JSON, so no new dependency is needed.
alternatives: Parse .tf files with an HCL parser dependency
decisions.tradeoffs: Users must run terraform show -json first; links through skipped resources (service → target group → LB) are not followed yet.

decisions.title: Drift is the import in sync mode, matched by id or label
decisions.why: One code path for import and drift keeps type mapping, link detection and grouping identical; running it on a copy gives the report, running it on the design adds the missing items as one unseen step, so the reviewer stays in control.
alternatives: Store a source address on each part for exact matching
decisions.tradeoffs: Only reports what the design lacks, not parts the infrastructure dropped; a rename on one side shows up as a new part.

decisions.title: Share as one self-contained HTML file, not a hosted link
decisions.why: The tool is local and single-user; a file with the app and data inlined can be attached to a PR or put on any static host with no server, accounts or auth. Reusing the built app (with an in-memory API) keeps steps, diff, flows and drill-down identical to the real app.
decisions.tradeoffs: The file is about 2 MB because it carries the whole app; it needs a fresh `npm run build` after app changes; readers can try edits but nothing is saved.

decisions.title: Static capacity and reachability analysis, not a traffic simulator
decisions.why: The design already carries qps on lines; summing incoming qps against a per-part capacity and re-walking the graph without a failed part answers 'what saturates' and 'what breaks' with no new data model or runtime. It runs in lint, so badges and agents get it for free.
alternatives: Propagate load automatically from entry points
decisions.tradeoffs: Load is only what the lines say (no fan-out math, retries or caching hit rates); a failure is all-or-nothing reachability, no partial degradation or timeouts.

decisions.title: Record an import source on parts instead of matching by name only
decisions.why: Name matching broke on renames and could not tell which design parts the infrastructure owns, so dropped resources went unreported. A source like terraform:aws_lb.public gives exact matching and a safe removal set.
alternatives: Keep name matching and report every unmatched part as removed
Separate mapping file per infra file
decisions.tradeoffs: Designs drawn by hand get sources only on their first sync (by name); two infra files of the same format against one design would remove each other's parts.

decisions.title: Follow Terraform references through undrawn resources with typed rules
decisions.why: Real stacks connect parts through resources that are not drawn (target groups, listeners, task definitions, event source mappings). Walking directed references through ordinary resources, joining wiring resources by which end is a front door, and never walking IAM, security groups or networks gives the expected lines without linking everything to everything.
decisions.tradeoffs: Wiring types are a fixed list (mostly AWS); unknown wiring stays unlinked, and the walk stops after three hops.

decisions.title: Map parts to C4 by type, one software system per design
decisions.why: Structurizr and C4-PlantUML need people, systems and containers; the design has only typed parts. Users become people, third-party types external systems, the rest containers of one system named after the design, with datastore and queue shapes. Boundaries become groups.
alternatives: Let the user pick a C4 role per part
Export as a system landscape only
decisions.tradeoffs: Designs that span several systems flatten into one; Network and Software-kit parts export as plain containers.

decisions.title: Tags as views instead of saved named views
decisions.why: Structurizr-style views mostly answer 'show me the parts about X'. A tag on the part answers that with no second structure to keep in sync: every tag in use is a view, and it follows the part through renames and moves.
decisions.tradeoffs: A view is one tag at a time (no AND/OR), and the choice is not saved in the design or the URL.

decisions.title: Read trace files offline instead of querying a tracing backend
decisions.why: A file works the same from the UI, the drift CLI and MCP, without credentials or network access. It keeps the app local and dependency-free, and CI can drift-check a captured sample.
alternatives: Query the Jaeger/Tempo HTTP API directly
decisions.tradeoffs: Numbers come from whatever sample was captured. qps is calls over the capture window, latency is half the caller's median, and the flow is walked from one sample trace. Traces never remove parts, because a missing service may simply not have been sampled. Only JSON is read; protobuf exports need converting first.

decisions.title: One importer, merged into the open design as a new step
decisions.why: Pasting is the cheapest way to bring diagrams in from other tools. Adding each paste as a new step keeps it reviewable and lets it be undone. Reusing parts by name lets a paste extend a design instead of duplicating it. The UI paste and the MCP tool share one code path, so they behave the same.
alternatives: Import only into new designs (as before)
Match parts by Mermaid node id
decisions.tradeoffs: Matching by name can join two different parts that share a name. Node ids are not used for matching, because hand-written diagrams use A, B, C. New parts take positions from a fresh full layout, so they can overlap parts placed by hand until Layout runs. Lines through architecture-beta junctions are reported, not resolved.
